title: Filippo Maria Visconti to Francesco Sforza, cipher slips of Nov 1446 - Mar 1447 (BnF italien 1583, 1584; key DECODE R5323)

steps.what: Mazzatinti's inventory of BnF ital. 1583-1593 marks 21 of the Duke's letters 'In cifre: membran.', three with a translation after them.
Gallica blocks scripts; the openapi.bnf.fr IIIF image API serves ital. 1584 full size. The ark recorded for ital. 1583 is a 1456 volume, so its six slips were taken from DECODE R7902-R7915.

Re-fetched the 15th-c. key records of ASMi Carteggio Sforzesco cart. 1597 (R5301-R5340) and read the headings; no. 23 (R5323) is headed 'Filippo Maria Duca di Milano'. f. 8 line 1 deciphers sign for sign to its translation f. 9.
ff. 8 and 5 deciphered and compared token by token with the translations ff. 9 and 6: 96.9% and 96.5% agreement; differences are the translator normalising Lombard spelling.
ff. 30/31, 36/37, 64/65 deciphered (95.5-98.9%); each pair is one letter sent twice. Their later clear copies (ff. 29, 35, 63) were found first and were in view.
ff. 23/24, 72 and 102 deciphered with no clear text; the two encipherments of ff. 23/24 fill each other; padding identified at the end of each slip.
Samples of ff. 83 and 94 deciphered first, then compared with their later clear copies: 99.2% and 98.5%; Mazzatinti's "copia moderna" f. 92 is the text of f. 94.

ital. 1583 ff. 130, 136, 158 deciphered from the DECODE images (88-92%); ff. 154 and 110 read in part after baseline-tracked re-transcription and, for the f. 110 verso, removal of the recto show-through.
Web search for an edition or decipherment of the slips or of the Duke's keys: none found; Cerioni 1970 covers the later Sforza period.

A parallel session found the same key a second time on DECODE R1857 image 17 (ASMi Potenze Sovrane cart. 1592, "Filippo Maria Duca di Milano") and calibrated it on ff. 5/8 against ff. 6/9 (96.7% / 97.8%); its corrections are in peer/working_key.md. Tomokiyo had tied R1857 (image 11) to ital. 1584 f. 69 only.

The BnF Archives et manuscrits record for ital. 1583 gives only microfilm MF 16151: the volume is not digitised (the ark btv1b10033686w is ital. 1587). The "Copie moderne di documenti" volumes are: ital. 1597 btv1b10037396j, 1598 btv1b10037380f.

ital. 1597 canvases 116-182 hold 19th-c. copies numbered with the ital. 1583 document numbers: f. 110 (canvases 126-127), f. 112, f. 136 (canvas 157), f. 145 (canvas 160); none of ff. 130, 154, 158. The f. 110 copy writes gi for the cipher group II+3 and leaves the blank name sign blank: it was made by deciphering the slip.

f. 110 re-transcribed line by line at 3.5-8x and aligned with the ital. 1597 copy: recto 96.5%, verso 69.6% of non-null signs (this folder's blind pass had read 32%). f. 136 likewise: 95.7%; the blind pass (91.5% by sense) matches the copy on only 68% of words.

lattice.py: beam search over candidate values for the glyph classes the binarized DECODE scans do not separate, scored with it-cinquecento order 5, tried on f. 136 where the copy fixes every value: 70 of 126 ambiguous signs right (55.6%). Not applied.

The survey of ital. 1584 by the parallel session showed that ff. 23/24, 72 and 102, read here as having no clear text, have one: f. 25 and f. 103 are contemporary decipherments, f. 73 a later copy (f. 103 had been taken for a parallel letter and used as a guide to sense in the f. 102 retry). Transcribed and compared: word agreement 83-88% with spelling variants, 64-73% exact.

Osio, Documenti diplomatici tratti dagli archivj milanesi III (1872) prints agents' reports, Sforza to the Duke of 12 Dec and the Pusterla procuration of 22 Dec 1446, none of the Duke's cipher letters.

outcome.fraction_read_source: texts/f*_tokens.tsv, all cipher tokens of the 19 slips (nulls counted as not read; ff. 83 and 94 sampled)
outcome.notes: 16637 tokens transcribed, 329 nulls, 1275 unread. Sixteen of the nineteen slips have a decipherment of the time or a later copy (ital. 1584 next to each slip; ital. 1583 ff. 110 and 136 in ital. 1597); only ff. 130, 154 and 158 are deciphered here with no clear text reached. ff. 110 and 136 were merged from a parallel session. f. 15 (key R5324) is written up as visconti1447.

gaps.item: f. 110 verso (1 Nov 1446): 231 signs run together on the binarized DECODE image (the 1597 copy gives the sense)
f. 72: the name signs < and est (the later copy f. 73 leaves < blank too)
ital. 1583 f. 145 (1 Dec 1446; its 19th-c. copy is ital. 1597 canvas 160) and the translation f. 131: ital. 1583 is not digitised (microfilm MF 16151)

texts.label: f. 110, Milan, 1 Nov 1446
texts.summary: After the rout of his army the Duke gives up his grudge: Sforza’s kind brief has changed his mind, he will never act against Sforza’s state, offers to pay his provision if Venice stops it and to send horse at his own cost, except against the Church and the King of Aragon, and asks for a quick conclusion.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 130, Milan, 25 Nov 1446
texts.summary: Sforza's brief of 14 November came by Perino da Cotignola; Cosimo de' Medici has always been well disposed; the Duke begs Sforza to come at once and dispose of the men-at-arms and of his own person, and to say whether he will stay in the Marche or come to Lombardy. The contemporary translation f. 131 exists but was not reached.

reading_review.note: sentences hold where read; holes in several sentences

texts.label: f. 136, Milan, 29 Nov 1446
texts.summary: The Duke sent Giovanni del Maino to Sforza with full powers the day after his letter of the 15th, but Sforza's men-at-arms in Cremona and the Cremonese have gone over to the enemy camp; it is more honourable to win than to sit in winter quarters.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 154, Milan, 12 Dec 1446
texts.summary: Donino has come from Sforza; the Duke is sending Pietro da Pusterla and Antonio da Trezzo to him secretly, awaits answers from the Pope and King Alfonso, and begs Sforza to conclude at once and in secret; letters are to go secretly through Cotignola.

reading_review.note: sentences hold where read; holes in several sentences

texts.label: f. 158, Cusago, 31 Dec 1446
texts.summary: After the rout of his men-at-arms the Duke sent Thomase to France for help: nothing but words from the Duke of Savoy, but the Dauphin is willing, and Asti has been offered to him in return; the Duke asks Sforza's opinion.

reading_review.note: sentences hold where read; holes in several sentences

texts.label: f. 5, Abbiategrasso, 10 Jan 1447
texts.summary: Reply to Sforza's letters and Pietro da Pusterla's: the Duke has worked to keep the Marquis of Mantua from Venice; if Rolando Pallavicino comes to terms with Venice he only does his duty; the Duke will follow Sforza's advice.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 8, Abbiategrasso, 11 Jan 1447
texts.summary: The Duke asks Sforza to send one of his most trusted men, seemingly as if he had left Sforza's service, through whom Sforza will know everything done at court, since nothing is to be done without his consent; even the Duke's worst enemy will do.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 24, Milan, 5 Feb 1447
texts.summary: Answer to Sforza's brief brought by Fra Benedetto da Valenza: the report from Cremona of a proclamation sparing Cremona is untrue and malicious; the Duke approves Sforza's writing to Cremona; on Foschino's request through Pietro Visconti at Pizzighettone.

reading_review.note: made before the clear text was found; words agree with it 64.4% / 84.1% (exact / with spelling variants)

texts.label: f. 23, Milan, 5 Feb 1447, duplicate of 24 Feb
texts.summary: The same letter as f. 24, enciphered afresh with other homophones and re-sent on 24 February ("duplicata die vigesimo quarto eiusdem").

reading_review.note: made before the clear text was found; words agree with it 65.4% / 83.2% (exact / with spelling variants)

texts.label: f. 30, Milan, 9 Feb 1447
texts.summary: Ser Battista, chancellor of the castellan of Castel Sant'Angelo, has come to Sforza for the Cardinal Camerlengo; the Duke is delighted and urges Sforza to deal with men trusted by the "Signori", since the Camerlengo can do everything with the Pope.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 31, Milan, 9 Feb 1447, duplicate of 24 Feb
texts.summary: The duplicate of f. 30, re-sent on 24 February.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 36, Milan, 12 Feb 1447
texts.summary: Asti is to be given to the Dauphin; Rolando Pallavicino; the missions of Gasparo degli Ubaldini and Giovanni del Maino; Cosimo de' Medici to urge Sforza to an agreement; a rumour that Sforza has renewed his pact with Venice hampers the raising of money.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 37, Milan, 12 Feb 1447, duplicate of 25 Feb
texts.summary: The duplicate of f. 36, re-sent on 25 February.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 64, Milan, 6 Mar 1447
texts.summary: Venetian troops have crossed the Oglio into the Cremonese to take Cremona; the Duke has sent Carlo Gonzaga, Alberto Pio and Conte Carlo with their men and the river fleet, and ordered Pietro Visconti at Pizzighettone to help save the town.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 65, Milan, 6 Mar 1447, duplicate of the same day
texts.summary: The duplicate of f. 64, sent the same day.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 72, Milan, 7 Mar 1447
texts.summary: Answer to four briefs of Sforza and a letter of Marcolino Barbavara: on binding himself to the Church and the King of Aragon Sforza should do as seems best and tell Marcolino; Pietro da Pusterla has gone to Ferrara; a request brought by Angelo Simonetta.

reading_review.note: made before the clear text was found; words agree with it 72.8% / 88.3% (exact / with spelling variants)

texts.label: f. 83, Milan, 11 Mar 1447
texts.summary: The Dauphin and Asti through Tommaso da Bologna; Rome and the Cardinal Camerlengo; Padua or Verona offered to the Duke of Ferrara; the Malatesta condotte; the Count of Urbino's planned raid; discontent in Milan with the agreement.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 94, Milan, 18 Mar 1447
texts.summary: The Duke is glad Sforza sent Messer Nicola Maffeo; praises his letters to the College of Cardinals and the governor of the March and the truce with the Malatesta; asks how he should write from now on.

reading_review.note: coherent; checked against the clear text

texts.label: f. 102, Milan, 23 Mar 1447 (duplicate)
texts.summary: The new pope, Nicholas V, will not do what he ought; Sforza should come to an understanding with the King of Aragon and act before the pope sets his feet more firmly.

reading_review.note: made before the clear text was found; words agree with it 70.2% / 87.5% (exact / with spelling variants)

prior.where: contemporary decipherments on the next leaf of eight of the eleven ital. 1584 letters (ff. 6, 9, 25, 38, 84, 95, 103) and of ital. 1583 f. 130 (f. 131, not digitised); later fair copies of every ital. 1584 letter (ff. 7, 10, 26, 29, 35, 63, 73, 82/85, 92, 101); 19th-c. copies of ital. 1583 ff. 110, 136 and 145 in BnF ital. 1597, made by deciphering the slips. None known for ff. 154 and 158.

human: The project chose the target from the Oct 2026 Venice/Milan sweep and asked for the slips to be read; the model found the key, mapped the volumes, and transcribed and deciphered the slips through worker subagents, checked by the main session.
